title: AWR/2 bundle
description: NON-NORMATIVE. JSON Schema is a convenience for tooling and is not the normative definition of AWR/2; awr/SPEC.md is (Appendix B). Where this schema and the specification disagree, the schema is the bug. A bundle is the transport container that profiles L1 and L2 and chain resolution need, because those require more than one document (SPEC.md §9).
$comment: SPEC.md §9: a bundle is NOT signed and carries no claims of its own; every claim inside it is verified individually, so passing this schema says nothing about any contained document beyond its shape. Two §9 rules are not expressible here: duplicate `id` values with differing content (AWR-BUNDLE-002), and identification of the subject document — a verifier MUST NOT depend on order and MUST identify the subject either by explicit caller argument or as the single WorkReceipt not referenced as anyone's parent, reporting AWR-BUNDLE-003 on ambiguity rather than guessing. Media type is application/json (§15), file extension .awrb.json (non-normative). §13.4: bundle processing is attacker-influenced work; implementations SHOULD bound total input size and nesting depth before canonicalizing.

awrBundle.$comment: SPEC.md §9: MUST be "2.0" (AWR-BUNDLE-001). Note that this is "2.0", not the documents' `awrVersion` of "2.0.0"; the two version strings are deliberately different lengths in the specification and are not interchangeable.

documents.$comment: SPEC.md §9: MUST be a non-empty array of AWR documents (AWR-BUNDLE-001). `oneOf` over the three document schemas is exact rather than merely convenient: each document schema requires its own AWR type and forbids the other two (§3.1, AWR-DOC-005), so no valid document can satisfy two branches, and a document with no AWR type or with two satisfies none.
